sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. In the petition it is stated that on 16.12.2015 at about 1.00 pm petitioner was rider one TVS Moped bearing reg. No.KA-13-V-5194 on the extreme left side of the Arasikere- Hassan road slowly by observing traffic rules, when he reached near Harohalli Kodimata, Kasanahalli hobli, Arasikere taluk, one Tractor
bearing
Regn No.KA-13-TA-2274 & Trailer bearing Reg.no.KA-13-TA-2275 driven by its driver
in a rash and negligent manner overtook the petitioner's moped and then came to left side of the road at high speed and suddenly stopped without any indicator or signal.

Due to which,
moped of the petitioner touched the backside of the tractor-trailer.
Inspite of best efforts made by the petitioner to stop his moped thereby petitioner fallen down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was shifted to Janpriya hospital, Hassan and admitted as inpatient (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.4839/2021 on 16.06.2015.

It is notice that, he sustained nasal bone fracture, facial injury,
multiple abrasions and other injuries all over the body.
He was discharged on 24.12.2015 after necessary treatment.
He has spent Rs.1,00,000/- for treatment, conveyance, medicine and other incidental charges.

He is suffering from permanent disability, getting severe headache, giddiness,
numbness and difficult to breath sometimes, no sensation of smell, ugly scars over the face and cannot do any mental strain work.
He totally lost normal activities of life.
Before the accident he was hale and healthy doing agriculture, sericulture and milk vending business by which, he was earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was contributing the said money to his family.
After the accident, he sustained financial loss as he could not work and disability is coming in the way of his day to day activities.

Arasikere Rural police have registered case in Crime No.264/2015 against the driver of tractor-trailer for the offence p/u/s 279 and 337 of IPC and after investigation charge sheet is filed against him.
1st respondent is R.C owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of tractor and trailer.
Therefore, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest @ 12% p.a in the above case.

sentences.text: 4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 owner is served.
He appeared through his counsel, but no written statement is filed.
Respondent 2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement.
He contended that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
He denied issuance of insurance policy in respect of tractor and trailer.
But contended that his liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
1st respondent not complied provisions of Sec.134(c) and police have not complied 158(c) of IMV Act.
The manner of accident is denied.
It is stated that the driver of said tractor had no D.L at the time of accident.
That insured or any one else have not informed this insurance company regarding the accident.
The manner in which petitioner narrated the accident is denied.
Medical expenses and treatment taken by the petitioner are denied.
Age, occupation and income of the petitioner are denied.
That in case of compensation granted, interest cannot exceed Rs.6% p.a.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
He relied upon following judgments (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.4839/2021 (i) NWKSRTC V/s Sonappa Rudrappa Kuravinkoppa M.F.A No.2973/2005, Honb'le High Court of Karnataka at Bangalore.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors- in-office has framed following:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner prove that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in a moor vehicle accident occurred on 16.12.2015 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tractor- Trailer bearing Regn No.KA-13-TA-2274 & KA-13- TA-2275 which hit TVS Moped No.KA-13-V-5194?
2. Whether the petitioner prove his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the 2nd respondent proves that the driver of Tractor-Trailer bearing Regn No.KA-13- TA-2274 & KA-13-TA-2275 did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident?

sentences.text: 4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5 . What Order or Award?
6. To prove his case, petitioner is examined as P.W.1.
Ex.P.1 to P.10 documents are marked on his behalf.
Doctor by name (SCCH-12) 6 MVC.No.4839/2021 K.M.Kumarswamy is examined as P.W.2 and through him Ex.P.11 and 12 documents are marked.
Petitioner evidence is closed.
On respondent side no evidence is led.
7. Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.
Both side submitted citations.
Counsel for 2 nd respondent has submitted written arguments.

8. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3: In the Affirmative, Issue No.4: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.5: As per final order,
for the following;
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1: As per the petition averments accident took place on 16.12.2015 at about 1.00 pm when petitioner was riding his Moped, one tractor-trailer moving in front of him, suddenly stopped and he hit behind the trailer and sustained injuries.
To prove this fact, he entered into the witness box.
He has produced FIR, first information, final report, wound certificate, spot panchanama, IMV report and discharge summary at Ex.P.1 to 6 and 9.
Wound certificate shows he was admitted to Janapriya hospital, Hassan on 16.12.2015 i.e., on the date on which accident said to have been taken place.
In the wound certificate it is mentioned as history of RTA on (SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.4839/2021 16.12.2015.
The wounds sustained by the petitioner as per the said document are nasal bone fracture, facial injury, abrasion etc.
It stated that injury no. 1 and 2 are grievous in nature.

First information is given by the brother of the petitioner stating that he received phone call from one Manjunatha stating that his brother Eshwarappa, petitioner sustained accident near Harohalli, near Kodimata road.
First informant is not eye witness but, he has given information to police on the basis of phone call received.
It is stated in the first information that driver of the tractor trailer was nelignet in driving since he stopped the vehicle suddenly without giving any indication.
On the basis of said information, Arasikere rural police registered crime in Crime No.264/2015 against the driver of tractor and trailer for the offence p/u/s 279, 337 of IPC and Sec.187 of ImV Act.
It is stated that, the driver of the tractor went away from the spot after causing accident.

After investigation charge sheet is filed against the same driver by name Doddegowda B.S stating that he was not having driving licence of tractor and trailer and owner of the said tractor has given the vehicle to the person who had no D.L.
Further, the driver was said to be negligent and offence under Sec.279, 338 of IPC registered against him along with Sec.180, 177 and 187 of IMV Act.
As per the IMV report, the moped sustained severe damages and on the tractor and trailer no visible damages are found.
The accident was not due to any mechanical defect of both the vehicles.

sentences.text: Further, respondent has denied issuance of policy as well as manner of accident alleged by the petitioner.
But, he has cross examined P.W.1 though he has stated that he has not issued the policy.
In cross examination of P.W.1 he has not mentioned anything about not issuing the policy in respect of tractor and trailer.
If he had not issued the policy he had no business to proceed with the case by cross examining the P.W.1.
He should have sought for deleting him from the case.
But, without questioning anything about the policy, he denied the manner of accident and attributed negligence on part of the petitioner in riding the two wheeler.
He denied the medical expenses and stated that sketch is not produced by the petitioner only to shadow the facts of the accident.
He asked about the delay in filing the petition stating that though accident took place in 2016 why petition is filed in 2021.
P.W.1 stated that driver of the tractor told him that he would bear the expenses but subsequently did not bear the same.
Therefore, petitioner was constrained to file the petition.
Except his there is no cross examination on the point of issuance of policy in respect of the vehicle involved in the above case nor there is dispute regarding the involvement o the vehicle.
The manner of accident alleged by the petitioner is denied by this respondent has not stated that how the accident took place,.
Neither the driver, nor the owner of the opponent vehicle is examined by the respondent No. 2 to show that the manner of accident explained by the petitioner is incorrect.
The FIR and final report are not questioned by the owner of driver.

Hence, on the basis of oral and documentary evidence, petitioner has proved that he (SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.4839/2021 sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 16.12.2015 from the rash and negligent driving of the tractor and trailer mentioned in the petition.
Hence, I hold this Issue in the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
Respondent no. 2 disputed the age of the petitioner.
To prove his age petitioner produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P.10 which shows that he was born on 19.07.1970.
Accident took place on 16.12.2015.
He was aged 45 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 45 years at the time of accident.
12. In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was an Agriculturist, doing sericulture and milk vending business and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
To prove this fact he has not produced any document.
Therefore, notional income has to be taken.
The accident took place in the year 2015 and Petitioner being resident of Arasikere taluk, Hassan District.
it is proper to consider his income at Rs.9,000/- per month.
Hence monthly income of the petitioner is held as Rs.9,000/-.
13. In respect of permanent disability a doctor by name K.Kumarswamy is examined as P.W.2.
He is Professor and Head of the Department of Dentistry, Bowring Hospital, Bengaluru
Doctor has assessed the disability of petitioner on 20.03.2023.

In his chief examination he stated that he has found mobility of teeth 5% disability and disocclusion of the posterior teeth 5% and sensitivity of teeth 5% and he has assessed the disability of total of 15% of whole body.
In the cross examination of P.W.2 his competency to assess the (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.4839/2021 disability is disputed, but he denied the same.
He stated that when petitioner was injured he was 42 years and now he is aged 58 years.

It is suggested to him that as per the guidelines issued by the government no disability can be given in respect of teeth and this witnesses stated that he has given disability as per American guidelines.

Now, it is necessary to notice that in the wound certificate Ex.P.4 it is mentioned about Eshwarappa Alias H.B. Eshwarappa vs Javare Gowda on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66770601/
5 nasal bone fracture and there is no mention about loss of teeth.

sentences.text: That apart, petitioner being agriculturist having milk vending business, the disability if any in teeth will not in any way come in the way of his occupation.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court there is no functional disability that can be attributed to the petitioner.
Therefore, no compensation can be awarded for loss of future income due to disability.
Accordingly I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.3 :
Respondent no.2 has admitted the insurance policy.
But he contended that the driver of the aforesaid tractor and trailer had no driving license and permit to run the tractor and trailer.

To prove this fact, 2 nd respondent has not examined any witness on his side, but the charge sheet on which petitioner relied about the accident itself contains the offence of having no DL by the driver of tractor and owner is charged for the said offence.
Hence on the basis of police documents produced by the petitioner himself, the said fact is proved even in the absence of specific defence evidence on that aspect.
The owner has not appeared and produced permit and DL of the driver to say contrary to final report.
Therefore, in the (SCCH-12) 11 MVC.No.4839/2021 opinion of this court, owner 1 st respondent has violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and then recover the same form the owner of the vehicle on the principle of pay and recover.
Therefore non-existence of D.L to the driver of the said vehicle is proved.
Hence, I answer this issue in the "Affirmative".
15. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the Tractor bearing Regn No.KA-13-TA-2274 & Trailer bearing Reg.no.KA-13-TA-2275.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings: The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries as per the wound certificate produced by him.
The records show that he underwent operation.
He was in hospital from 16.12.2015 to 24.12.2015 and wound debridement and suturing was done and POP was applied.
Therefore, he sustained pain and sufferings.
For pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- .
(ii) For Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.7.
Totally he has paid amount of Rs.88,233/- as per Ex.P.7medical bills.
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
They are subsequent to the date of accident.
Though they are disputed, no satisfactory (SCCH-12) 12 MVC.No.4839/2021 material is placed to disbelieve the bills.
They are supported by prescriptions of the dotor.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.88,233/-.
(iii) For Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was admitted in Janapriya hospital, Hassan on 16.12.2015 and discharged on 24.12.2015.
He was in hospital for almost 09 days .
Accident took place in the year 2015.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.200/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.

Hence for food and nourishment Rs.200/- x 09 days = Rs.

6 1,800/-is awarded.

sentences.text: (iv) For Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 09 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence per day if Rs.200/- is awarded as attendant charges in 2015, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.200/- x 09 days =Rs.1,800/-is awarded.
(v) For Loss of income during laid up period: As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is. Rs.9,000/-.
He was inpatient for 09 days and he was advised to take rest.
Minimum 2 months is required to recover from such operation in view of grievous injury.

Therefore,
laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 2 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.9,000/-x (SCCH-12) 13 MVC.No.4839/2021 2= 18,000/- He is entitled to Rs.18,000/- as loss of income during laid up period.
(vi) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner was shifted to Janapriya hospital, Hassan and subsequently he went for further follow-up treatment.
He has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.
Considering all those conveyances, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.5,000/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
(vii) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given to issue no.2 there is no functional disability that can be attributed to petitioner which would cause loss of future income.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded towards loss of future income due to disability.
(viii) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :

As per the evidence of assessed doctor,
petitioner complained about pain and restriction in movement.
He suffers discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
He suffered facial injury and abrasion.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and came in the way of normal enjoyment of life.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.

Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
(ix) For Future medical expenses:
P.W.2 has not stated anything about necessity of future medical treatment hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-

sentences.text: Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.1,74,833/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
16. ISSUE NO.5:-

In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,74,833/- with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Further it is held that, after such deposit, respondent no.2 insurance company is entitled to recover the said amount along with interest from respondent no.1 on the principle of Pay and Recovery.
The petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation along with interest without making F.D.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
in a rash and negligent manner overtook the petitioner's moped and then came to left side of the road at high speed and suddenly stopped without any indicator or signal.
He was discharged on 24.12.2015 after necessary treatment.
After the accident, he sustained financial loss as he could not work and disability is coming in the way of his day to day activities.
Therefore, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
He denied issuance of insurance policy in respect of tractor and trailer.
1st respondent not complied provisions of Sec.134(c) and police have not complied 158(c) of IMV Act.
opennyai_summary.arguments: But contended that his liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner prove that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in a moor vehicle accident occurred on 16.12.2015 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tractor- Trailer bearing Regn No.KA-13-TA-2274 & KA-13- TA-2275 which hit TVS Moped No.KA-13-V-5194?
2. Whether the petitioner prove his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the 2nd respondent proves that the driver of Tractor-Trailer bearing Regn No.KA-13- TA-2274 & KA-13-TA-2275 did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5 . What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the basis of said information, Arasikere rural police registered crime in Crime No.264/2015 against the driver of tractor and trailer for the offence p/u/s 279, 337 of IPC and Sec.187 of ImV Act.
As per the IMV report, the moped sustained severe damages and on the tractor and trailer no visible damages are found.
The accident was not due to any mechanical defect of both the vehicles.
Eshwarappa Alias H.B. Eshwarappa vs Javare Gowda on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66770601/
4 (SCCH-12) 8 MVC.No.4839/2021 10.
If he had not issued the policy he had no business to proceed with the case by cross examining the P.W.1.
Neither the driver, nor the owner of the opponent vehicle is examined by the respondent No. 2 to show that the manner of accident explained by the petitioner is incorrect.
The FIR and final report are not questioned by the owner of driver.
Hence, on the basis of oral and documentary evidence, petitioner has proved that he (SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.4839/2021 sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 16.12.2015 from the rash and negligent driving of the tractor and trailer mentioned in the petition.
To prove this fact, 2 nd respondent has not examined any witness on his side, but the charge sheet on which petitioner relied about the accident itself contains the offence of having no DL by the driver of tractor and owner is charged for the said offence.
Hence on the basis of police documents produced by the petitioner himself, the said fact is proved even in the absence of specific defence evidence on that aspect.
The owner has not appeared and produced permit and DL of the driver to say contrary to final report.
Therefore, in the (SCCH-12) 11 MVC.No.4839/2021 opinion of this court, owner 1 st respondent has violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and then recover the same form the owner of the vehicle on the principle of pay and recover.
Therefore non-existence of D.L to the driver of the said vehicle is proved.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.
The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings: The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries as per the wound certificate produced by him.
He was in hospital from 16.12.2015 to 24.12.2015 and wound debridement and suturing was done and POP was applied.
As per the findings given to issue no.2 there is no functional disability that can be attributed to petitioner which would cause loss of future income.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded towards loss of future income due to disability.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
(ix) For Future medical expenses:
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-
 (SCCH-12) 14 MVC.No.4839/2021  Particulars of Heads In Rs.
i. Pain & Sufferings 30,000/-
ii.
Total Rs. 1,74,833/-
Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.1,74,833/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,74,833/- with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Further it is held that, after such deposit, respondent no.2 insurance company is entitled to recover the said amount along with interest from respondent no.1 on the principle of Pay and Recovery.
The petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation along with interest without making F.D.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
